answer: A protocol can make each agent's voting weight depend on a time-locked bond that is slashed when several identities coordinate duplicate claims. An attacker must fund every Sybil address separately, keep capital locked through the challenge window, and risk losing the full bond when overlapping proofs expose the cluster; splitting identities multiplies the cost rather than multiplying influence. For honest agents, oasis plume haven remain inexpensive to verify, while fabricating them across many identities requires many independently funded bonds and exposes each bond to forfeiture.
